general.title: TV wall mounting
general.jobDescription: Mount a 55-inch TV on the living room wall with a tilting bracket and hide the cables. Customer has already bought the bracket.
general.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We'd love to help get your 55-inch TV mounted up on the living room wall with your tilting bracket and those cables neatly tucked away. Here's what we're putting together for you.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a breakdown of the materials we'd be looking at for this job:

• Cable trunking 16mm x 16mm white (qty: 10) — to conceal TV cables along wall [Price TBC]
• Wall plugs 10mm (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Masonry screws 6x60mm (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• HDMI cable 2m (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Power cable extension 2m (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Cable clips adhesive 20mm (qty: 1) [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Check the wall type and locate studs or solid fixing points suitable for supporting a 55-inch TV.
• Mark and drill fixing holes, then fit wall plugs and masonry screws to secure the tilting bracket firmly to the wall.
• Attach the bracket arms to the back of the TV and carefully hang it onto the wall plate.
• Route the HDMI cable and power extension cable neatly from the TV down to the nearest connection points.
• Fix cable trunking along the wall to fully conceal the cables for a clean finish.
• Secure any remaining cable runs using adhesive cable clips where trunking isn't used.
• Test the tilt function and confirm the TV is sitting level and feels secure before we're done.

ASSUMPTIONS
• The wall is masonry and in sound condition, suitable for secure bracket fixing.
• You'll have the tilting bracket ready on the day — we'll take it from there!
• The work area will be clear and easy to get to, with a nearby power socket available.
• No plastering or redecorating is included if cable routing leaves any surface marks.

EXCLUSIONS
• The tilting bracket itself isn't included — you've already got that covered, which is great!
• Any plastering, filling, or repainting of the wall after the install isn't part of this quote.
• If we find any unexpected issues behind the wall (like awkward noggins or hidden pipes), any extra work needed would be quoted separately.
• Electrical socket installation or repositioning isn't included here.

plumber.title: Kitchen tap repair
plumber.jobDescription: Kitchen mixer tap dripping from the spout and won't turn off fully. Customer would rather repair it than replace it.
plumber.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We've put this quote together to cover the repair of your kitchen mixer tap, which is dripping from the spout and not closing off fully. We're happy to help get it working properly again rather than replacing it.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
• Ceramic disc tap cartridge 1/2" (spline count — 20 or 24 to be confirmed once old cartridge is removed) — [Price TBC]
• Adjustable wrench (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]
• Plumber's grease — [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Isolate the water supply to the kitchen mixer tap before starting work.
• Remove the tap handle and dismantle the cartridge housing using an adjustable wrench.
• Extract the existing ceramic disc cartridge and check the spline count so the correct replacement can be matched and sourced.
• Inspect the tap body and valve seat for any corrosion or damage while the cartridge is out.
• Fit the new 1/2" ceramic disc cartridge, applying plumber's grease to the seals during reassembly.
• Refit the tap handle and restore the water supply.
• Run the tap and check thoroughly for leaks or dripping before finishing up.

ASSUMPTIONS
• We're assuming the water supply to the tap can be isolated locally or at the stopcock without any issues.
• We're assuming the tap body and valve seat are in sound condition — if there's hidden corrosion or damage, that could change things.
• We're assuming clear access to the sink and under-cabinet area will be available on the day.
• The exact cartridge spline count will be confirmed once the old one's removed.

EXCLUSIONS
• Replacement of the full tap if the body turns out to be damaged or a matching cartridge can't be sourced.
• Any repairs to water-damaged cabinets, worktops or flooring around the sink.
• Reseating the valve if the seat itself is worn — that's a separate job.
• Callout costs for a return visit if parts need ordering after the initial inspection.

[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We'd love to help you transform your bathroom — this quote covers stripping out your existing suite and fitting a new bath with overhead shower, close coupled toilet, and vanity basin in the same layout.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a breakdown of the materials we'll be using for your bathroom — everything's been chosen to get the job done properly and leave you with a finish you'll love!

• Acrylic bath 1700mm x 700mm (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]
• Thermostatic bar mixer shower (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]
• Close coupled toilet (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]

• Tanking kit (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

• Strip out the existing bath, toilet and basin, and remove all old tiles and fittings ready for the new suite.
• Dispose of the old suite, tiles and waste materials — likely a skip or van runs, so we'll confirm the best option with you.
• Apply tanking to the shower and wet areas, then fix tile backer boards to the walls where tiling is planned.

electrician.title: Consumer unit replacement
electrician.jobDescription: Old fuse box with rewireable fuses in the under-stairs cupboard of a three-bed semi. Replace with a modern consumer unit with RCD protection, about 8 circuits.
electrician.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We've put this quote together for replacing your old rewireable fuse box in the under-stairs cupboard with a modern consumer unit, covering around 8 circuits. We're really looking forward to helping you get this sorted.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a rundown of the materials we'll be using for this job:

• Consumer unit 10-way RCBO (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]
• RCBO 32A Type A (qty: 2) — [Price TBC]
• RCBO 6A Type A (qty: 2) — [Price TBC]
• Surge protection device (qty: 1) — [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Remove the existing rewireable fuse box from the under-stairs cupboard and safely disconnect all circuits
• Supply and fit a new 10-way RCBO consumer unit with individual RCBO protection on each circuit
• Install 2 × 32A Type A RCBOs and 2 × 6A Type A RCBOs for the relevant circuits
• Fit a surge protection device within the new consumer unit
• Reconnect all existing circuits and carry out testing to confirm they're performing as expected
• Check main earthing and bonding conductors are adequate for the new installation
• Inspect existing cable condition before reconnecting — any old rubber or cloth-covered wiring will be flagged before we proceed
• Identify and report any hidden faults uncovered during testing, such as borrowed neutrals, which would need resolving before the board can be energised

ASSUMPTIONS

• We'll keep the consumer unit in its current under-stairs position, so no extra cable runs are needed.
• The property will need to be without power for most of the working day.
• Clear, unobstructed access to the cupboard will be available throughout.

EXCLUSIONS
• Any repairs to faults found on existing circuits during testing — we'll flag these and quote separately if needed.
• Rewiring circuits or extending cable runs if the board position changes.
• Any work to the meter, supply fuse, or anything on the supply side of it.
• Hidden issues like borrowed neutrals or undersized earthing, should these come to light during testing.

NEXT STEPS

carpenter.jobDescription: Replace 5 internal doors with white primed shaker doors in a 1990s house, reusing the existing frames. New hinges and handles on each.

[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We're putting this quote together to cover swapping out your five internal doors for new white primed shaker doors, fitting fresh hinges and handles throughout, and making the most of your existing frames.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
• Internal door white primed shaker 762mm x 1981mm (qty: 5) — [Price TBC]
• Butt hinges 76mm (qty: 10) — [Price TBC]
• Lever door handles on rose (qty: 5) — [Price TBC]

roofer.title: Slipped roof tiles
roofer.jobDescription: Several slipped and broken concrete tiles on the back slope of a two-storey house, causing a small leak into a bedroom ceiling.
roofer.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We've put this quote together to cover the repair of several slipped and broken concrete tiles on the back slope of your two-storey home, which should help get that bedroom ceiling leak sorted out.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a breakdown of the materials we're looking at for your roof repair — everything's itemised clearly so you know exactly what's going into the job:

• Concrete interlocking roof tile (qty: 5) — to replace slipped and broken tiles on the back slope [Price TBC]
• Tile clips (qty: 5) [Price TBC]
• Treated roofing batten 25mm x 50mm (qty: 2) — if battens are found to be rotten under the missing tiles [Price TBC]
• Breathable roofing membrane (qty: 10) — if battens are replaced [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Inspect the back slope of the roof from a suitable access platform or ladder to identify all slipped, cracked, and broken concrete tiles.
• Carefully lift and remove damaged tiles, taking care to avoid putting unnecessary load on surrounding tiles.
• Check battens beneath the affected area for rot or damage before proceeding with tile replacement.
• Replace any rotten battens and lay breathable roofing membrane beneath where battens are renewed.
• Fit up to five new concrete interlocking tiles with tile clips to secure them properly in position.
• Re-bed or re-point any disturbed areas as needed to ensure a weathertight finish.
• Clear all debris from the roof and gutters on completion and leave the site tidy.

ASSUMPTIONS
• We're assuming the roof battens and felt beneath the damaged tiles are sound — if they've deteriorated, additional materials and time will be needed.
• We're assuming we can source matching concrete interlocking tiles — older profiles can sometimes be tricky to find.
• Clear, safe access to the rear of the property is assumed to be available on the agreed day.
• Internal ceiling repairs aren't included in this quote.

EXCLUSIONS
• Any repairs to your bedroom ceiling or redecorating after the leak — that's a separate trade.
• Wider roof work if we find the tile nails have failed more broadly across the slope.
• Sourcing reclaimed tiles if the existing concrete pattern turns out to be discontinued.
• Any additional tiles accidentally broken during access to the repair area.

decorator.jobDescription: Repaint walls, ceilings and woodwork in two double bedrooms. A few cracks to fill, and colours are similar to what is there now.
decorator.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We'd love to help freshen up your two double bedrooms — filling those cracks and repainting the walls, ceilings, and woodwork throughout. It's going to make a real difference.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a rundown of the materials we'll be using for the job — everything's been picked to give you a really solid, lasting finish:

• Trade matt emulsion white 10L (qty: 2) — for walls in two double bedrooms [Price TBC]
• Ceiling matt emulsion white 5L (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Satinwood paint white 2.5L (qty: 1) — for woodwork (doors, frames, skirting) [Price TBC]
• Fine surface filler (qty: 1) — for crack filling [Price TBC]
• Decorators' caulk (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Cotton dust sheet (qty: 2) [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Protect floors and any remaining furniture in both bedrooms with cotton dust sheets, and mask off edges and trim with 50mm masking tape.
• Clean all walls, ceilings and woodwork down with sugar soap to remove grease and dust before any painting begins.
• Fill cracks and imperfections with fine surface filler, then sand back smooth using medium and fine sanding sponges once dry.
• Apply decorators' caulk to any gaps around frames and skirting for a neat, clean finish.
• Apply two coats of trade matt emulsion to the walls in both rooms, allowing full drying time between coats.
• Apply two coats of ceiling matt emulsion to both bedroom ceilings.
• Apply two coats of satinwood to all woodwork, including doors, frames and skirting boards.

ASSUMPTIONS
• Walls and ceilings are sound and need only minor filling and sanding — no plaster repairs are included.
• Colours are similar to what's there now, so two coats should give a great finish.
• Furniture will be moved away from the walls before we arrive, giving us clear access to work.
• Inside cupboards and built-in wardrobes aren't included unless we've agreed otherwise.

EXCLUSIONS
• Moving or repositioning heavy furniture — we'll need clear access to the walls before we start.
• Plaster repairs beyond minor crack filling — anything more substantial would need to be quoted separately.
• A third coat if colours turn out to need more coverage than expected.
• Painting inside any wardrobes or cupboards.

builder.title: Kitchen–dining knock-through
builder.jobDescription: Remove the wall between the kitchen and dining room in a 1930s semi to make one open-plan room. The wall is likely load-bearing and will need a steel beam.
builder.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We'd love to help you open up that kitchen and dining room into one lovely space. Here's our quote for removing the wall and installing a steel beam to make it happen.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
• Steel universal beam (size to be confirmed by structural engineer) — [Price TBC]
• Concrete padstone 440mm x 215mm x 100mm (qty: 2) — [Price TBC]
• Fire resistant plasterboard 12.5mm 2400mm x 1200mm — [Price TBC]
• Bonding plaster 25kg — [Price TBC]
• Multi-finish plaster 25kg — [Price TBC]
• Metal angle bead 2.4m (qty: 2) — [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Carry out a full structural assessment of the wall with a structural engineer to confirm it's load-bearing and size the steel beam before any work begins.
• Sheet off the rest of the house to contain dust and protect your belongings — knocking through a 1930s wall creates a lot of mess.
• Install temporary props and acrow supports to carry the ceiling and floor above while the wall comes out.
• Remove the existing wall carefully, checking for any hidden pipework or wiring as we go.
• Bed the concrete padstones onto engineering bricks at each beam end, pack level with steel packers, and lift the steel beam into position.
• Box in the steel beam using fire-resistant plasterboard and finish with angle bead, bonding plaster, and multi-finish plaster to blend with the surrounding surfaces.

ASSUMPTIONS
• A structural engineer's beam size calculation will be provided before work begins.
• The foundations beneath both ends of the wall are adequate to carry the new beam.
• Floor levels on either side of the wall are roughly even — any significant difference may need addressing separately.
• Clear access to the kitchen and dining room will be available throughout, with the rest of the house sheeted off to contain dust.

EXCLUSIONS
• Structural engineer's calculations and building control fees — you'll need to arrange those separately.
• Moving any electrics, pipework or radiators found inside the wall once it's opened up.
• New flooring across the old wall line.
• Decorating — plastering will be left ready for you to paint.

NEXT STEPS
• Give this quote a read-through and let us know if you're happy to go ahead — we're ready when you are!

gardener-landscaper.title: Sandstone patio
gardener-landscaper.jobDescription: Lay an Indian sandstone patio at the back of the house, replacing part of the lawn. Customer wants a slight fall away from the house.
gardener-landscaper.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We're really looking forward to helping you transform that back garden — we'll be lifting the existing lawn and laying a beautiful Indian sandstone patio with a gentle fall away from the house to keep everything draining nicely.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
• Indian sandstone paving slab (for patio surface) — [Price TBC]
• MOT type 1 sub-base bulk bag (for patio foundation) — [Price TBC]
• Weed control fabric 1m x 10m — [Price TBC]
• Slurry primer for natural stone — [Price TBC]
• Sharp sand bulk bag — [Price TBC]
• Concrete edging kerb (to edge patio where it meets remaining lawn) — [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Mark out the patio area and strip back the existing lawn and topsoil to the required depth.
• Excavate and compact the sub-base using MOT type 1 to create a stable foundation.
• Lay weed control fabric over the compacted sub-base before any bedding material goes down.
• Bed the Indian sandstone slabs on a sharp sand and cement mix, with slurry primer applied to the back of each slab to ensure a solid bond.
• Set the patio with a gentle fall away from the house so rainwater drains off naturally.
• Install concrete edging kerbs along the boundary where the new patio meets the remaining lawn.
• Clean down the finished surface and remove all excavated soil and waste from site.

ASSUMPTIONS
• We're assuming the ground beneath the turf is firm and stable once the topsoil's been dug out.
• We're assuming the patio will sit at least 150mm below the damp-proof course on the house wall.
• We're assuming surface water can drain freely across the garden once the fall is in place.
• We're assuming clear access to the back garden is available throughout the job.

EXCLUSIONS
• Removal or repositioning of any drain covers or manholes within the patio area.
• Any drainage channel next to the house wall — we'll check the damp-proof course level on the day, but this would be a separate cost if needed.
• Planting, reseeding, or tidying the lawn edges around the new patio.
• Disposal of excavated soil and turf — skip hire or removal can be arranged separately.

plasterer.title: Ceiling board and skim, 4m × 4m
plasterer.jobDescription: Living room ceiling about 4m x 4m with several long cracks. Board over where needed and skim, ready to paint. Room will be cleared.
plasterer.content:
[YOUR BUSINESS NAME] | [YOUR CONTACT DETAILS] | Date: [DATE]

Thanks so much for getting in touch! We'd love to help get your living room ceiling looking great again — we'll be boarding over the damaged areas and skimming the whole ceiling smooth, so it's all ready for painting once you are.

MATERIALS & EQUIPMENT
Here's a breakdown of the materials we'll be using for your job — everything's been selected specifically for the work we've scoped out together:

• Plasterboard 12.5mm 2400mm x 1200mm (qty: 2) — to board over damaged ceiling areas [Price TBC]
• Plasterboard screws 50mm (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Scrim tape (qty: 1) [Price TBC]
• Multi-finish plaster 25kg (qty: 2) [Price TBC]

Prices to be confirmed — contact for a full material cost breakdown.

SCOPE OF WORK
• Clear and protect the work area (room will be cleared by you ahead of our visit — thanks for that!).
• Inspect the ceiling to confirm joists are sound and identify which areas need boarding over.
• Fix two sheets of 12.5mm plasterboard over the damaged sections using 50mm plasterboard screws.
• Apply scrim tape over all joints and edges where new board meets the existing ceiling.
• Skim the entire ceiling with two coats of multi-finish plaster to a smooth, paint-ready finish.
• Feather and blend skim edges so the surface is level and consistent across the full ceiling.
• Leave the finished plaster to dry fully — new plaster will need several days before it's ready to paint.

ASSUMPTIONS
• The room will be cleared and ready to work in, as you've mentioned — that's a big help, thanks!
• Any previous leak has been fixed and the ceiling has fully dried out before we start.
• The ceiling joists are sound and able to support new plasterboard where needed.
• New plaster will need several days to dry out completely before it's ready to paint.

EXCLUSIONS
